title: Limit of an inverse system of complexes with ML terms and essentially constant H^{-1} (Stacks 070E)
statement:
For an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] $(B_i)_{i\ge1}$ of abelian groups (transition homomorphisms $B_{i+1}\to B_i$, hence composites $B_k\to B_i$ for $k\ge i$) let $\varprojlim_iB_i=\{(x_i)\in\prod_iB_i: x_{i+1}\mapsto x_i\}$. The system is *Mittag-Leffler* (ML) [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system] if for every $i$ there is $c(i)\ge i$ with $\operatorname{Im}(B_k\to B_i)=\operatorname{Im}(B_{c(i)}\to B_i)$ for all $k\ge c(i)$. It is *essentially constant* [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system] if there are an abelian group $X$ with homomorphisms $X\to B_i$ compatible with the transition maps, an index $i_0$ and a homomorphism $B_{i_0}\to X$ such that $X\to B_{i_0}\to X$ is the identity and for every $j$ there is $k\ge\max(i_0,j)$ such that $B_k\to B_j$ equals the composite $B_k\to B_{i_0}\to X\to B_j$.

Now let $(A^{-2}_i\xrightarrow{d^{-2}_i}A^{-1}_i\xrightarrow{d^{-1}_i}A^0_i\xrightarrow{d^0_i}A^1_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an inverse system of complexes of abelian groups ($d^{j+1}_id^j_i=0$; transition maps $A^j_{i+1}\to A^j_i$ commuting with the $d$'s), let $A^j=\varprojlim_iA^j_i$ with the induced complex $A^{-2}\to A^{-1}\to A^0\to A^1$, let $H^j_i=\ker d^j_i/\operatorname{im}d^{j-1}_i$ ($j=-1,0$) with the induced inverse systems, and let $H^{-1},H^0$ be the corresponding cohomology groups of the limit complex. If $(A^{-2}_i)$ and $(A^{-1}_i)$ are ML and $(H^{-1}_i)$ is essentially constant, then the canonical map $H^0\to\varprojlim_iH^0_i$, $[(x_i)_i]\mapsto([x_i])_i$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For the tower $K$, put $A^j=K\mathbin{\circ}\mathrm{eval}_j$, $Z^j=K\mathbin{\circ}\mathrm{cycles}_j$ and $H^j=K\mathbin{\circ}\mathrm{homology}_j$ (Lean indices $0,1,2,3$ represent degrees $-2,-1,0,1$). The natural transformation $p_j:Z^j\to H^j$ is termwise epic. Construct $B^j=\ker p_j$ in the functor category, with inclusion $b_j:B^j\to Z^j$, and $q_j:A^{j-1}\to B^j$ by lifting the differential-to-cycles map. At each index that differential-to-cycles map has cokernel $p_j$ by Mathlib homologyIsCokernel. Termwise exactness and injectivity of $b_j$ show $q_j$ is epic. Thus $B^j$ is the boundary system without choosing an arbitrary witness. The kernel sequence of $p_j$ is termwise short exact. Also $0\to Z^{j-1}\to A^{j-1}\xrightarrow{q_j}B^j\to0$ is termwise short exact: its kernel is the kernel of the differential because $q_jb_j$ followed by the cycles inclusion is that differential. These are cycleSequence, boundarySequence and their proved private helpers.

proof.text: Prove directly that cycles preserve the limit of $K$. Given a cone into the cycle tower, compose its legs with the cycles inclusions, lift it to the limit of the degree-$j$ terms, and use the degree-$(j+1)$ limit projections to prove that this lift is killed by the differential. Factor through cycles of the limit. Cancellation of the cycles inclusions and the universal property of the termwise limit prove factorization and uniqueness. Hence $z:\mathrm{cycles}_j(\lim K)\to\lim Z^j$ is an isomorphism (cycles_preservesLimit).

proof.text: If $f:A\to B$ is an epic morphism of towers and $A$ is ML, apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] to the termwise short exact kernel sequence $0\to\ker f\to A\to B\to0$. Thus $B$ is ML. Apply this to $q_{-1}$ and $q_0$: both boundary towers $B^{-1}$ and $B^0$ are ML by the two termwise ML hypotheses [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. This is the helper ml_of_epi.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-sequence-ml] to $0\to B^{-1}\to Z^{-1}\xrightarrow{p_{-1}}H^{-1}\to0$. Its kernel is ML by Step 3 and its quotient is essentially constant [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system] by hypothesis. Therefore $Z^{-1}$ is ML (ml_middle_of_exact).

proof.text: Apply part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] to $0\to Z^{-1}\to A^{-1}\xrightarrow{q_0}B^0\to0$, whose first tower is ML by Step 4. Obtain an epic map $\lim q_0:\lim A^{-1}\to\lim B^0$. Since the degree-$-1$ evaluation also preserves limits, this is precisely the surjectivity needed to identify boundaries of the limit complex with $\lim B^0$.

proof.text: Apply part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact] to $0\to B^0\to Z^0\xrightarrow{p_0}H^0\to0$, whose first tower is ML by Step 3. Its limit is short exact. The existing theorem already includes left exactness, so no module-category tower exactness or change of coefficients to $\mathbf Z$ is needed.

proof.text: Let $h$ be the asserted limit.post map, $z$ the cycles comparison of Step 2, and $a$ the evaluation comparison in degree $-1$. Projection identities give $\pi h=z(\lim p_0)$ and $d_{\mathrm{cycles}}z=a(\lim(q_0b_0))$. Since $z$ is invertible and $\lim p_0$ is epic, the first identity proves $h$ is epic. For injectivity, represent a class killed by $h$ by a cycle $y$. Exactness in Step 6 gives $b\in\lim B^0$ mapping to $z(y)$. Surjectivity in Step 5 lifts $b$ to $v\in\lim A^{-1}$. The second identity and injectivity of $z$ identify $y$ with the boundary of $a^{-1}(v)$, so its class is zero. Thus $h$ is both mono and epi in abelian groups, hence is an isomorphism. All identities and element lifts are proved in homology_comparison_of_ml_cycles; instantiate at Lean indices $i=1,j=2$.
